locator: 16.18-19, 18.17-18 and 28.16-20, with John 20.21-23 and 21.15-17, Dei Verbum §19 and Lumen gentium III §§19, 22 for the historicity and institutional content of the commissions
goal: The bridge STMT-BRIDGE-CHRISTS-CHURCH-FOUNDED-BY-GOD is derived (CATHOLICISM-BRIDGE-DIVINE-FOUNDING-FROM-ATTESTED-MANDATE) from STMT-RESURRECTION-CONFIRMS-JESUS-MANDATE (Acts 17.31, Acts 2.22-36), STMT-GOD-CONFIRMS-ONLY-TRUTH (Dei Filius ch. 3 para. 1), STMT-MANDATE-COVERS-JESUS-FOUNDING-WITH-TEACHING and STMT-ENVOY-FOUNDING-IS-GODS-FOUNDING (John 13.20). The scope premise is derived (CATHOLICISM-MANDATE-SCOPE-FROM-CATHOLIC-CHURCH-FOUNDING) from stage 6 and STMT-MANDATE-COVERS-JESUS-FOUNDING-OF-CATHOLIC-CHURCH, which is in turn derived (CATHOLICISM-NARROW-SCOPE-FROM-COMMISSION-REPORTS) from the report-to-event premise STMT-COMMISSION-REPORTS-GO-BACK-TO-JESUS (Matthew 28.18-20 and at least one of Matthew 16.18-19, 18.17-18, John 20.21-23, 21.15-17 go back to Jesus; Dei Verbum §19) and STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES (Lumen gentium §§19, 22). Next obligation, the 'institution or message' fork, which is now split between two open premises: a rival may deny the link premise STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES (the second omission model has every commission going back to Jesus and no founding in the mandate, with the message rival true), or, granting the link premise together with Jesus' mandate and his founding of the Catholic Church as a visible society with authority, must deny each of the four governing commissions (Commissions.messageRival_denies_governing_reports). Defend both: STMT-COMMISSION-REPORTS-GO-BACK-TO-JESUS historically, and STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES as the reading that such a conferral is the institution of the Church (Lumen gentium §§19, 22 assert it; the claim that one power or a promise suffices is unattributed). Pinned critical witnesses: Harnack, History of Dogma I, ch. II §3, note 76 dates the words of Matthew 16.18 and 18.17 later (STMT-MATT-16-18-18-17-SAYINGS-LATER); Renan, Life of Jesus ch. XVIII, states as a possibility that many words on binding and remitting were attributed to Jesus (STMT-COMMUNITY-ATTRIBUTION-OF-CHURCH-POWERS-POSSIBLE). Neither denies a power outright. CATHOLICISM-MESSAGE-RIVAL-EXCLUDED-BY-ATTESTATION shows that a rival granting the link premise, Jesus' mandate and his founding of the Catholic Church as a visible society with authority, must deny STMT-JOHN-COMMISSION-INDEPENDENT-OF-MATTHEW or STMT-HEAVEN-RATIFIED-ATTESTATION-CRITERION (multiple attestation of the heaven-ratified family, Matthew 16.19, 18.18 and John 20.23); both are unsourced and wait for a witness: a pinnable or read source stating the criterion of multiple attestation (Burkitt 1906; Meier, A Marginal Jew I, ch. 6) and one on John 20.21-23's relation to Matthew (Dodd 1963; Brown's Anchor Bible John), and a critical source denying 16.19, 18.18 or John 20.23 outright. Galatians 2.7-9 is pinned as a passage and read (ATTEMPT-GOVERNING-COMMISSION-ATTESTATION; non-discriminating, no claim). Secondary: a source analysing envoy agency beyond reception for STMT-ENVOY-FOUNDING-IS-GODS-FOUNDING (Aquinas on mission), and Romans 1.4 for attestation. Do not use Dei Filius ch. 3 para. 5's direct assertion as a premise. See docs/founding-authorization-source.md.
reason: The 'institution or message' fork is split between a historical report-to-event premise, supported only by a doctrinal witness (Dei Verbum §19), and the institutional link premise; granting the link premise, Jesus' mandate and his founding of the Catholic Church as a visible society with authority, the message rival must deny John's independence or the multiple-attestation criterion for the heaven-ratified family, and neither of those premises nor their denials is yet sourced.
